medications.dose: Start 500 mg PO nightly with evening meal; after 1 week increase to 500 mg BID; titrate by 500 mg weekly to target 1 g BID (2 g/day) as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after any change in renal function
medications.purpose: Improve insulin sensitivity and prevent progression to type 2 diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 (type 2 diabetes prevention) and CG181 recommend metformin as first‑line for high‑risk pre‑diabetes

medications.duration: Lifelong — lipid profile at 3 months, then review annually
medications.purpose: Primary prevention of cardiovascular disease in metabolic syndrome (QRISK ≥ 10 % or multiple risk factors)
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 / PH46 advise statin therapy for adults with QRISK ≥ 10 % or metabolic‑syndrome components

contraindications.reason: Risk of lactic acidosis in severe renal impairment (NICE NG28 contraindication)
contraindications.alternative: Use DPP‑4 inhibitor (e.g., sitagliptin) if eGFR <30 and glucose lowering needed

contraindications.reason: Fluid retention and risk of heart failure (contraindicated in heart failure per NICE NG28)
contraindications.alternative: Avoid; consider GLP‑1 RA for weight management if needed

contraindications.reason: May worsen glucose tolerance and mask hypoglycaemia (NICE CG181 contraindication)
contraindications.alternative: Use ACE‑I or CCB if hypertension treatment becomes necessary

contraindications.reason: Can worsen glucose tolerance and dyslipidaemia (NICE CG181 contraindication)
contraindications.alternative: Prefer ACE‑I or low‑dose thiazide only if required

assumptions_warnings: eGFR/renal function not provided – assume eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m² before starting metformin; order serum creatinine/eGFR.
Lipid profile and QRISK score not available – calculate QRISK and obtain fasting lipid panel to confirm need for statin intensity.
Liver function tests not provided – obtain ALT/AST before initiating statin and any future Orlistat.
Allergy history unknown – confirm no hypersensitivity to metformin or statins.
Blood pressure recorded only once (127/80 mmHg) – repeat measurements on two separate occasions before initiating antihypertensive therapy.
Alcohol intake not recorded – screen for excess alcohol which may affect NAFLD and medication safety.
treatment_summary: Start metformin 500 mg nightly with titration to 2 g/day (if eGFR ≥30) and atorvastatin 20 mg nightly for primary CVD prevention, alongside intensive lifestyle modification (diet, exercise, weight‑loss programme, smoking/alcohol advice). Monitor renal function, liver enzymes, lipid profile, HbA1c and blood pressure at recommended intervals. Re‑evaluate in 4–6 weeks for drug tolerance and lab results; adjust therapy based on QRISK, eGFR, and weight loss response.
